name: InterContinental - ANA Tokyo
insider_take: This towering luxury landmark in Akasaka has been Tokyo's diplomatic hub since 1983, where world leaders and celebrities have sealed deals over sake.
whats_special: The hotel sits directly above Tameike-Sanno Station, making it incredibly convenient for exploring Tokyo. Its Pierre Gagnaire à Tokyo restaurant holds a coveted Michelin star, while the 36th-floor Club InterContinental Lounge offers breathtaking views of Tokyo Bay and Mount Fuji on clear days. The property uniquely blends Japanese hospitality with international luxury standards.
pro_tip: Book a room on floors 30-36 for spectacular city views, and time your Club Lounge visit for sunset cocktails when Tokyo's skyline transforms into a glittering wonderland.
dont_miss: The Imperial Palace East Gardens are just a 10-minute walk away, perfect for morning jogs among cherry blossoms. Ginza's luxury shopping district is two subway stops away, while the nearby Hie Shrine offers a peaceful escape with its famous red torii gates cascading down stone steps - a hidden Instagram gem most tourists overlook.
pros: Prime Akasaka location with easy access to Tokyo's top business districts, embassies, and cultural landmarks
Stunning panoramic views of the Tokyo skyline and iconic Tokyo Tower from upper-floor guest rooms
World-class dining with multiple acclaimed restaurants offering both Japanese and international cuisine
Exceptional service rooted in Japanese hospitality traditions, consistently praised for attentiveness and professionalism
Spacious, elegantly appointed rooms and suites blending contemporary design with refined comfort
cons: Premium luxury pricing may not suit budget-conscious travelers
Primarily business and upscale traveler-focused atmosphere, which may feel formal for leisure-only guests
